c.tagline: Faded colonial charm at the gateway to the Bijagós Islands.

taxi.fareNote: Shared 'town taxis' run fixed routes with fixed per-seat fares (roughly 300-600 CFA); private hire or airport trips are negotiated in cash beforehand since meters aren't used.

emergency.note: Emergency response is very limited nationwide and medical facilities are basic; contact your embassy and travel-insurance assistance line for serious problems.

hood_landmark.Bissau Velho (Old Town): Fortaleza de São José da Amura, Bissau

hood_desc: The weathered Portuguese colonial quarter around the old port and the São José da Amura fortress, rich in history but with limited tourist infrastructure — for history-minded, adventurous travelers.

The city's real center of gravity, lined with government buildings, banks, and most of Bissau's hotels and restaurants around the Presidential Palace — the easiest, most practical base for any visitor.
A calmer, largely residential and commercial district just inland from downtown, favored by NGO staff and longer-stay visitors who want quiet streets close to the center.
A sprawling, densely packed working-class quarter built around West Africa's famous Bandim market — vibrant and authentic, but with almost no visitor amenities.
The corridor along the road to Osvaldo Vieira Airport, increasingly home to newer hotels and aparthotels aimed at business travelers wanting a quick airport run.

water.note: Tap water is not considered safe to drink; use bottled or treated water.

transit.pay: There is no formal ticketing system; pay the driver or tout in cash (CFA francs) on boarding toca-tocas and shared taxis, and agree private taxi fares verbally before the ride since meters aren't used.
transit.hours: Informal daytime service roughly 6am-9pm; little to no scheduled transit after dark, though private taxis can usually be hailed or phoned at night.
transit.note: Bissau has no metro, tram, or formal city bus network — getting around relies on shared minibuses (toca-tocas), shared taxis, and private taxi hire.

bus: Shared bush taxis and minibuses to regional towns (Bafatá, Gabú, Cacheu)
Long-distance routes to Ziguinchor, Senegal and Conakry, Guinea
ferry: Inter-island boats and pirogues from the Port of Bissau to the Bijagós Archipelago (Bubaque, Orango, and other islands)

airport.name: Osvaldo Vieira International Airport (OXB)
rentals: No major international rental chains operate at OXB; hotels and local travel agencies arrange car-with-driver hire

tip.r: Not customary or expected; rounding up the bill or leaving small change at restaurants and for taxi drivers is appreciated but not required.
